'''Constantin S. Teleman''' (born in 1968)<ref>{{cite book |title=Quantum field theory and manifold invariants |date=2021 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |location=Providence |isbn=978-1-4704-6123-2 |page=iv}}</ref> is a Romanian-American mathematician. He studies [[algebraic geometry]], [[algebraic topology]], [[Lie group|Lie groups]] and [[Loop quantum gravity|loop groups]] as well as their representations and their connections to [[mathematical physics]], notably [[quantum field theory]].

Teleman began studying at [[Harvard University]] in 1987 (that same year, he was a Putnam Fellow<ref>{{cite web |title=1987 Putnam Competition Results |url=https://kskedlaya.org/putnam-archive/putnam1987results.html |website=kskedlaya.org |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref>) and obtained his master's degree in 1991.<ref name="cv">{{cite web |title=Constantin Teleman - UC Berkeley Department of Mathematics |url=https://math.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/constantin-teleman |website=math.berkeley.edu |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref> He then received his doctoral degree in 1994 under the direction of [[Raoul Bott]] (and [[Graeme Segal]] after he worked at the [[University of Cambridge]]) with a thesis titled "Lie Algebra Cohomology and the Fusion Rules".<ref name="MathGenealogy">{{cite web |title=Constantin Teleman - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=63055 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref> He was then the Szegö assistant professor at [[Stanford University]] and Research Fellow at St John's College at the University of Cambridge. In 1999, became an assistant professor at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] and lecturer in 2001,  then in 2003 a reader for St John's College at Cambridge. In 2007, he was a professor at the [[University of Edinburgh]]. He is now a professor at [[UC Berkeley]].<ref>{{cite web |title=People – Simons Collaboration on Global Categorical Symmetries |url=https://scgcs.berkeley.edu/people/ |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref>

== Prizes and honors ==
In 2002, he received the [[Whitehead Prize]] for his contributions to [[Representation theory|representations]] of infinite-dimensional groups, particularly loop groups. In 2015, he was a Senior [[Berwick Prize|Berwick prize]] laureat along with [[Dan Freed|Daniel Freed]] and [[Michael J. Hopkins]] for their article ''{{Lang|en|Loop groups and twisted K-theory}}''.<ref>{{cite web |title=List of LMS prize winners London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners |website=www.lms.ac.uk |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref> They proved the [[isomorphism]] between the twisted equivariant [[K-theory]] of a [[Lie group|compact Lie group]] and the Verlinde algebra of its loop group.<ref>{{cite web |title=Loop Groups and Twisted K-Theory in nLab |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Loop+Groups+and+Twisted+K-Theory |website=ncatlab.org |language=en}}</ref> In 2014, he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Seoul.<ref>{{cite web |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers {{!}} International Mathematical Union (IMU) |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine%3DNocedal=&combine=&order=field_speakers_congress_city&sort=asc&page=123 |website=www.mathunion.org |access-date=12 July 2025}}</ref>

==Selected publications==

* with [[Dan Freed|Daniel Freed]], ''"Relative Quantum Field Theory''", ''Commun. Math. Physics'', vol. 326, 2014, p. 459–476, [[arxiv:1212.1692|Arxiv]]
* with [[Edward Frenkel]], ''"Geometric Langlands correspondence near opers''", ''J. Ramanujan Math. Soc.'' 28 A, 2013, p. 123–147, [[arxiv:1306.0876|Arxiv]]
* ''"The structure of 2D semi-simple field theories''", ''Invent. Math.'', vol. 188, 2012, p. 525–588, [[arxiv:0712.0160|Arxiv]]
* with Daniel Freed, [[Michael J. Hopkins]], ''"Loop groups and twisted K-theory''", Volume 1, ''Journal of Topology'', vol. 4, 2011, p. 737–799, Tome 2, ''J. Amer. Math. Soc.'', vol. 26, 2013, p. 595–644, Tome 3,  ''Ann. of Math.'', vol. 174, 2011, p. 947–1007, [[arxiv:0711.1906|Volume 1, Arxiv]], [[arxiv:math/0511232|Volume 2]], [[arxiv:math/0312155|Volume 3, Arxiv]]
* with Daniel Freed, Michael J. Hopkins, [[Jacob Lurie]], ''"Topological Quantum Field Theories from Compact Lie Groups''", in P. R. Kotiuga (éd.), A celebration of the mathematical legacy of Raoul Bott,  AMS 2010, [[arxiv:0905.0731|Arxiv]]
* with Christopher T. Woodward, ''"The index formula for the moduli of G-bundles on a curve''". ''Ann. of Math.'', vol. 170, 2009, p. 495–527, [[arxiv:math/0312154|Arxiv]]
* with Susanna Fishel, [[Ian Grojnowski]], ''"The strong Macdonald conjecture and Hodge theory on the loop Grassmannian''", ''Ann. of Math.'', vol. 168, 2008, p. 175–220, [[arxiv:math/0411355|Arxiv]]
* ''"The quantization conjecture revisited''", ''Ann. of Math.'', vol. 152, 2000, p. 1–43, [[arxiv:math/9808029|Arxiv]]
